page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E2.2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on x86_64 AMD EPYC 7551 processors. The instance provides 2 physical cores running 2 threads per core, presenting 4 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. System memory totals 16.0 GB RAM, establishing a balanced memory-to-vCPU allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The VM.Standard.E2.2 configuration does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage, requiring remote block volumes for persistent data retention. It contains no GPU accelerators, reserving all computing tasks exclusively to the AMD host CPU. In terms of external connectivity, the server configuration includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Because it relies on first-generation AMD EPYC silicon clocked at 2.0 GHz, per-thread instruction throughput is modest compared to higher-clocked alternatives.

Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio and dedicated vCPU allocation, VM.Standard.E2.2 is positioned for general-purpose enterprise applications. Typical deployment profiles include intermediate web application servers, small-to-medium relational and caching datastores attached to network block storage, container hosts, build nodes, and background microservices that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or high-frequency clock speeds.
